overview: This study note explores the practical application of Romans 12, focusing on dedication through the concept of the living sacrifice, and the necessary relationships a Christian must maintain with God, fellow believers, and enemies.

topics.title: Four Therefores in Romans
topics.summary: Romans 12 has four 'therefore' statements that establish a chain of relationships, starting with the condemnation of the world, leading to justification, assurance, and finally, dedication.
key_points: Romans 3:20 is the 'therefore' of condemnation: the whole world is guilty before God.
Romans 12:1 is the 'therefore' of dedication, which is the basis for other relationships.

topics.title: Body as Living Sacrifice
topics.summary: Your body is a living sacrifice to give to God, exemplified by two living sacrifices in the Bible: Isaac and Jesus Christ.
key_points: Your body is a living sacrifice to give to God.
Isaac would have died in obedience to God, yielding to God’s will.
Jesus Christ actually died in sacrifice.

topics.title: Mind as Sacrifice
topics.summary: Your mind is a sacrifice to God, and the Holy Spirit changes your mind by releasing inner power, allowing you to be a transformer rather than a conformer.
key_points: The world wants to change your mind with external pressure.
The Holy Spirit changes your mind by releasing power within.
Meditating on God’s Word and memorization makes you more spiritual.

topics.title: Will as Sacrifice
topics.summary: Your will is a sacrifice to God, and yielding your will to God allows His power to take over, which gives us willpower through disciplined prayer.
key_points: Your mind controls your body, and your will controls your mind.
Yielding our will to God lets His power takeover, giving us willpower.
Pray about everything and yield the plans of the day to Him.

topics.title: Relationships with Believers
topics.summary: Christian relationships involve honest self-evaluation of spiritual gifts and faithful cooperation, while loving participation requires an attitude of joy, patience, and faithfulness.
key_points: Each Christian must identify spiritual gifts and ministry called to, ideally in a local church.
Be honest in evaluation; both under and over-evaluating are examples of pride.
Work with others even if you don't like them; no gift is better than another.
Gifts are tools to build with, not toys or weapons.
Love is the circulatory system of the spiritual body, requiring honest, humble love.
